text:
Maya: Quick heads-up — int8 bring-up for rwd-v6b finished. Before we promote to Dedicated/Demo, we need to finalize lease handoff semantics + automatic fallback thresholds. Observations: p95 ~1.12x baseline, hallucation +0.6% on our safety eval slice, cost ~-22%. Can we lock gates so infra can run a quiet burn?

Jon: Can you paste the A/B numbers and sample sizes?

Maya: Sure — baseline=v6a (fp16), canary=rwd-v6b-int8. sample=10k eval; live quick-sample = 2k. Short table: instr_acc 92.1 -> 91.4 (-0.7% abs), halluc 1.2% -> 1.8% (+0.6% abs), p95 120ms -> 135ms (+12.5%), error_rate 0.02% -> 0.03% (+0.01% abs). Cost delta -22% per token.

Emily: From the A/B logs: no spike in 5xx but a slight uptick in rerank mismatches on long-doc slice. Worth adding a long-doc slice watch.

Rachel: SRE note — our current SLOs say auto-fallback if error-rate >0.05% or p95 >1.5x baseline. But quality gates are product-level. I propose combined automatic fallback triggers: 
- instr_accuracy absolute drop >0.8%
- hallucination absolute increase >0.75%
- p95_latency multiplicative >1.4x
- error_rate absolute increase >0.03%
Any one should be enough to start a controlled rollback. Also require consecutive windows to avoid noisy blips.

Jon: +1. Operational plan: two-stage rollout: shadow -> quiet-burn 5% traffic for 6h. Metric windows: 30m for quality, 15m for infra. Hysteresis: require 3 consecutive windows breaching threshold to auto-fallback. Also implement a variant lease: lease_ttl=60m; infra renews on promote to avoid split-brain when multiple teams test same model.

Maya: Agreed. Add a cost-safety override: if cost per million tokens drops by >15% and all quality deltas are within thresholds, allow promote (with approval).

Emily: I'll sketch the rollout config we can push to model-config. Paste below — we should mirror this in the console UI too.

```yaml
promote_policy:
  canary_traffic: 0.05
  canary_duration: 6h
  metrics:
    - name: instr_accuracy
      type: absolute_drop
      threshold: 0.8
      window: 30m
      required_consecutive: 3
    - name: hallucination_rate
      type: absolute_increase
      threshold: 0.75
      window: 30m
      required_consecutive: 3
    - name: p95_latency
      type: multiplicative
      threshold: 1.4
      baseline: "model:v6a:p95"
      window: 15m
    - name: error_rate
      type: absolute_increase
      threshold: 0.03
      window: 15m
  lease_ttl: 60m
  fallback_actions:
    - route_canary_back_to_baseline
    - pause_autoscale_for_canary_pool
    - notify: ["#eng-oncall", "@model-owner"]
```

Jon: Fallback sequence looks good. Small ask: add a manual hold flag in console + require an explicit "approve_promote" for >20% traffic changes. Also we should tag the rollout with eval_snapshot id for traceability.

Maya: Will do. @deploy-bot please annotate upcoming rollout with eval:snapshot:20260320-12 and enforce the policy.

deploy-bot: rollout-automation: scheduled rollout id=r-20260321-42 (canary 5% at 2026-03-21T17:00Z). Automation will enforce the configured thresholds and lease TTL.

Emily: I'll open a tiny PR in model-config with the policy and add a commit message referencing r-20260321-42. Owner @Maya; reviewers @Jon and @Rachel.

Maya: Thanks — scheduling quiet burn for tomorrow 10:00 PT. If no objections by EOD I'll hit go. :thumbsup:

Rachel: LGTM from SRE, just ensure the alert runbooks link to the rollforward/rollback steps.

Jon: One last ops note — collect debug traces for any requests that hit rerank mismatch on long-doc slice and store under /var/model-onboard/traces/r-20260321-42.

Maya: Noted. Will follow up with a small runbook and attach to the rollout.

Emily: ping me if you want help wiring the console UI to show the required_consecutive windows.

Maya: Thanks all.
